subject: Intermittent upload truncation over private bridge — SYN-proxy MSS interaction
messages:
From: Arjun Mehta <arjun@bighealth.co>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+platform@bighealth.co
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upload failures to private deploy (intermittent)

Hi Kimberly —

We've had intermittent failures from our backup appliance to the Redwood private connector this morning. Large uploads (2–10MB files) from our on-prem backup node occasionally complete but the file on Redwood's side is truncated ~1400–1500 bytes less. Re-sends succeed maybe 30% of the time.

Symptoms we've observed:
- Client logs show final TCP ACKs but server reports truncated payload.
- Traces suggest a mid-path device might be modifying MSS or dropping fragments.
- Problem started after our vendor applied a packet inspection update at 03:00 UTC.

Attached a packet capture taken from our appliance and a short syslog excerpt. Can you confirm whether Redwood's private gateway is seeing reassembly failures or if any NAT behavior could be causing this?

Thanks,
Arjun
Network Engineer — BigHealth
attachments: bighealth-upload-fail.pcap
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Arjun Mehta <arjun@bighealth.co>, ops+platform@bighealth.co, netops@clearwave.io
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upload failures to private deploy (intermittent)

Thanks for the trace, Arjun — looping in infra and network on-call. Quick notes from my initial look:
- The capture shows TCP segments with MSS option reduced to 1360 in the SYN from the appliance, but later packets seem to be leaving with full 1500-sized payloads and getting ICMP frag-needed messages. That pattern smells like MSS clamping + a SYN proxy or DPI device rewriting TCP options.
- On our side, the Redis-based connector logs show a sequence gap at the same timestamps, then a hard close from the peer.

Action items for triage:
1) Vanessa/rishi: confirm whether the private gateway applied any intermediate NAT, synproxy, or MSS-clamp policies in the last 24–48h.
2) Priyom: can you request the ClearWave edge team check for SYN proxy or IDS signatures around the vendor update window?
3) Arjun: can you run a non-TCP-path MTU probe (tracepath or trace -M) and share results?

I'll collect runbook steps and an initial mitigation (accepting temporary MSS clamp on gateway) if needed.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
SRE, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Arjun Mehta <arjun@bighealth.co>, netops@clearwave.io
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upload failures to private deploy (intermittent)

Kim — we pushed a micro-update to the private gateway's edge rules last night (rate-limiting fix). No intentional MSS clamping on our side, but the vendor (ClearWave) did flip on an HTTP/TCP SYN-proxy feature recently in the same maintenance window — I didn't realize that would affect non-HTTP flows.

We asked ClearWave to confirm but their initial reply said the proxy is 'application-aware' and should only touch port 80/443. Given the capture, I want them to verify whether the proxy is also touching flows based on signature heuristics.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Disable SYN-proxy on the affected ClearWave edge for BigHealth (low-risk rollback).
- Temporarily enable MSS clamp at the private gateway to 1400 to avoid fragmentation.

I recommend we ask ClearWave to disable syn-proxy while we confirm. Priyom — can you escalate?

-Vanessa
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: netops@clearwave.io, ops+platform@bighealth.co, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Upload failures to private deploy (intermittent)

Hi ClearWave team —

Forwarding traces from BigHealth. We're seeing a pattern consistent with a SYN-proxy or DPI engine rewriting TCP options (MSS) during handshake, then an ICMP 'fragmentation needed' later in the path. That combination causes sender to transmit larger segments than path supports because the effective MSS negotiated was altered mid-handshake. Please confirm:
1) Was HTTP/TCP SYN-proxy or any connection normalization feature enabled for BigHealth during the 03:00 UTC maintenance window?
2) If enabled, can you temporarily disable it for the BigHealth circuit and confirm ASAP?

We can enable MSS clamping on the Redwood gateway as a stop-gap (runbook attached), but we'd prefer to eliminate proxy rewriting if it's touching non-HTTP flows.

-- Priyom

Hi all —

Confirmed: during the vendor maintenance window we enabled a new connection normalization profile that included a SYN-proxy for 'web-accelerate' signatures. Due to a classification bug the profile matched some non-HTTP TCP flows originating from the BigHealth backup appliance, which caused the SYN handshake to be terminated and re-originated by the proxy with a smaller MSS. Downstream, an MTU-limited link (a carrier MPLS hop we share with the customer) still delivered ICMP frag-needed, but because the proxy altered the handshake, the original sender didn't see the corrected path-MTU.

We've rolled back the normalization profile for the BigHealth circuit at 14:40 UTC and validated uploads from the appliance — three full uploads completed without truncation.

Root cause: mis-classifying non-HTTP flows into a syn-proxy profile + an MTU-limited mid-path hop.
Mitigation taken: disabled syn-proxy for the circuit; recommended Redwood enable MSS clamp to 1400 if the carrier hop remains MTU-constrained long-term.

We will follow up with a permanent fix (signature update) tomorrow. Apologies for the impact.

Regards,
ClearWave Operations
